clue.text: No interest in crane with red breast

indicators.note: the breast is the middle of the body, so the colour is placed in the middle of the crane word

parts.note: a boom is the long arm of a crane, here standing for the whole machine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher is unmoved by a crane with a red-breasted look.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird reading of 'crane' misleads: it is the machine, named by its arm. 'breast' places the colour in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is the state of having no interest in anything around you.

clue.text: Objecting to providing tipsy sister with gin cocktail

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters of sister are jumbled
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up too

explanation.surface: Someone protests at giving a drunken sister a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' turns SISTER into RESIST and 'cocktail' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposing or holding out against something is to be objecting to it.

clue.text: Fancy it will turn up in time

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the time word

parts.note: noon is a time of day

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the little word it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone imagines an item will appear eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'will turn up' reads the pronoun bottom to top; 'in' sets it inside the midday word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an idea or whim, a synonym of a passing thought.

clue.text: Provides firm leadership but, travelling as the crow flies, gets nothing right

parts.note: going as the crow flies is going by the straight, direct route
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A forceful boss goes straight to the point but achieves nothing correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a person: one who provides firm leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge of a company or a film gives the orders and leads.

clue.text: Vigorous struggles between rival campanologists?

parts.note: fierce fights, pictured whimsically as contests of bells sounding back and forth between rival teams of bell-ringers

explanation.surface: Two teams of bell-ringers fight it out.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers, and bells go 'ding' and 'dong'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for hard-fought, evenly matched contests with blows exchanged back and forth.

clue.text: Engineers laid up need this treatment

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing a kind of treatment

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word laid is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Bedridden engineers require some medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAID into DIAL. REME, the army engineering corps, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial care is corrective therapy meant to put a fault right.

clue.text: Clergyman may, having no income

indicators.note: read as in-come: the word no comes in, inside the verb

parts.note: can and may both express being allowed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vicar may find himself without any salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'income' must be split as 'in come': the negative comes in, inside the verb for may.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Medoc to be retailed within a month

indicators.note: within says the letters lie inside the run of words Medoc to be retailed

explanation.surface: A claret is due to go on sale in some month.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the calendar year, between September and November.

clue.text: Also acted as a guide in the city

indicators.note: the guiding word goes inside the word for also

parts.note: too means also
led means guided the way

explanation.surface: Someone also showed people round the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the guiding verb inside the word for also; the definition is just 'the city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic Spanish city, famed for its sword steel.

clue.text: To name, in another way

indicators.note: put another way, the letters of To name in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Phrasing the act of naming differently.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TO NAME IN gives the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose someone formally for a post is to name them.

clue.text: The wicked sit in a circle, engaged in calumny

indicators.note: sitting in something places one word inside the other

parts.note: a ring is a circle
evil is what is wicked

explanation.surface: Villains gather in a ring to slander someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit in' places the villains' word inside the circle word.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is slander, so someone abusing another verbally is engaged in it.

clue.text: River swirling around a Ubend

indicators.note: water swirling round churns, so the letters of a Ubend are mixed

explanation.surface: Water swirls round the bend in a plumber's pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major European river flowing to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Study movements on the floor then arrange postponement of payment for stock

definitions.text: arrange postponement of payment for stock

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a tango is a dance, a set of moves on the dance floor

explanation.surface: Learn some dance steps, then a stock-market deferral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: On the old London Stock Exchange this was the fee for carrying a settlement over to the next account.

clue.text: Early means of flood relief

parts.note: reads as old drainage engineering, but means the vessel that saved a family and the animals from the biblical Flood

explanation.surface: An ancient way of coping with floods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis a great vessel carried a righteous man, his family and the animals through the Deluge.

clue.text: Having quarrelled with another, young bird was injured

parts.note: a squab is a young pigeon
bled means lost blood from a wound

explanation.surface: A fledgling hurt itself fighting with a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker noisily with someone is to quarrel.

clue.text: To retreat is a disadvantage

explanation.surface: Pulling out of something is a bad move.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull away or withdraw is to draw back; as one word it means a downside or snag.

clue.text: Caught in Barking, up the creek?

definitions.text: Caught in Barking, up the creek?

parts.words: Caught in Barking, up the creek?
parts.note: pictures a creature trapped in Barking Creek, a tidal inlet in east London, suggesting a shellfish of royal name

explanation.surface: Something was netted in an east London backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London with Barking Creek running into the Thames; 'King' sits inside 'Barking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large horseshoe-shaped marine arthropod, a creature one might catch in tidal water.

clue.text: Chemical element that is without very good, superior content

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the abbreviation goes round the rest

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
top means excellent, the best

explanation.surface: A chemical substance is lacking a really good, high-class content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' has its old sense of outside here, so the abbreviation wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One of several forms of an element differing in neutron count, loosely a variety of that element.

clue.text: Dashing off with ease, say, toss it out

indicators.note: with here holds the sound inside the throwing word

parts.note: to fling something out is to toss it

indicators.note: say signals that what follows is heard rather than read

parts.note: the word ease said out loud matches two letter Es

explanation.surface: Someone runs off casually, tossing something aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns 'ease' into its sound, the letter E twice over; 'with' holds those inside the throwing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away in haste is dashing off from danger.

clue.text: Wire friend first, being in good humour

indicators.note: first puts the friend before the wire

parts.note: ami is French for friend
a cable is a wire, also an old word for a telegram

explanation.surface: Send a telegram to a pal first, while feeling cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts the French friend in front of the wire, though the clue names the wire first.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured, as in an amicable settlement.

clue.text: One doctor has information for her

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for a girl's name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MO is a medical officer
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A physician holds data about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gen' is British slang for information; MO is a medical officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a female forename, the heroine of Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: Purloin something from a poet

definitions.meaning: take something, here pilfer from someone
George ..., nineteenth-century English writer and verse translator

explanation.surface: Plagiarise a poet's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something for use is the verb; George Borrow is the English author and translator of ballads.

clue.text: incur damage of a mysterious kind

indicators.note: damage wrecks something, so the letters of incur are broken up

explanation.surface: Suffer harm from something eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes were secret ancient letters, so runic means cryptic or arcane.

clue.text: Difficulties when he leaves the money

indicators.note: when he leaves, those two letters depart from the word the

parts.note: taken as written
roubles are Russian currency

explanation.surface: Problems arise when a man walks off with the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems or worries are synonyms for difficulties.

clue.text: Collapse, due to moulting feathers

indicators.note: the shedding comes after the feathers, so it follows them

parts.note: down is soft feathering
a moult is the fall of old feathers

explanation.surface: A bird's decline is caused by losing its plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin or overthrow, as in the downfall of a government.

clue.text: Making the pupils work

parts.note: reads as a teacher setting a class tasks, but pupils are the dark centres of the eyes, put to use in watching

explanation.surface: A teacher keeps the class busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching or looking at something closely uses the eyes.

clue.text: Seek a cat, lost from the baker's

indicators.note: something lost is astray, so the letters of seek a cat are scrambled

explanation.surface: Searching for a cat that went missing from the bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasted buns with currants, sold at a bakery.
